summary: Georgia's oldest surviving coastal lighthouse: a 65-foot brick tower on Sapelo Island, lit in 1820 for the port of Darien, dark since 1905, now state land.

structures.note: 660 feet east of the tower (Section 8, p. 13); about 600 feet in the Section 7 description (p. 4); moved several times

access.note: State land inside the Sapelo Island National Estuarine Research Reserve; reached by the Reserve's ferry and tours.

facts.agency: State of Georgia (Sapelo Island National Estuarine Research Reserve)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1905. The nomination says the 1820 tower was deactivated in 1905 and that the station as a whole was deactivated in 1933; the Board's 1899 report shows the range lights put out by the October 1898 gale and relit within days. Both dates are kept in the story.
The 1820 contract, as the nomination quotes it, gives sixteen-inch reflectors; LighthouseFriends gives fifteen inches.
The nomination says the 1905 steel tower went to Southport, North Carolina; LighthouseFriends says South Fox Island, Michigan.
The nomination dates the state's full title to 1992; LighthouseFriends says the state and NOAA bought the southern 206 acres in 1991.

The archive roster and LighthouseFriends both list Robert H. Cromley as first assistant from 1890 to 1895; the nomination does not mention that stint. The nomination and the 1914 Bulletin place him as assistant from 1912. Neither source says whether the 1890-1895 stint and the 1912 stint are the same man.

notes_for_editor: Sources read: the NRHP nomination (1997, full text; printed page numbers checked against the PDF pages, which match the printed footers for pp. 7, 10, 13, 14); LighthouseFriends (facts only, paraphrased and cited); the Light-House Board reports for 1899 (entry 756, printed p. 117; table, printed p. 19, scan p. 29, checked on the page image: 'Lights extinguished owing to damage by gale October 2; reestablished October 13, 1898'), 1900 (entry 802, printed p. 111) and 1901 (entry 825, printed p. 124, scan p. 166, checked on the page image); the 1914 Lighthouse Service Bulletin (PDF p. 8; text matches); the Reserve's visitors page (cached; confirms the visitor center at Meridian and the public and group tours); the USLHS roster. The roster was matched to the USLHS place record 'Sapelo Island Range Rear' (0.4 km), which describes the 1820 light station (Darien, est. 1820, discontinued 1899 in the archive's fields); the roster lines are used as printed. SCAN PAGE NOT CONFIRMED: entry 802 (1900 report) is printed p. 111 per the OCR page headers; the archive's index gave scan p. 131, but the image service returned errors for that leaf and scan 111 is blank, so no scan page is cited. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, Georgia papers) found nothing usable for the station. Names taken from the archive roster are not confirmed in a primary record. DISAGREEMENTS LEFT FOR THE EDITOR: (1) reflectors: 16-inch (1820 contract as quoted in the nomination) vs 15-inch (LighthouseFriends). (2) Daymark date: 1869 (nomination's quote of the Board's 1869 report) vs about 1850 (LighthouseFriends). (3) Range beacon distance: 660 feet (Section 8) vs about 600 feet (Section 7), both from the nomination; LighthouseFriends says 660 feet southeast. (4) Steel tower destination: Southport, N.C. (5) Ownership: state title from the Reynolds heirs in 1992 (nomination) vs the state and NOAA buying the southern 206 acres in 1991 (LighthouseFriends).
